The refinement follows (immediate gate now SATISFIED as above):

# HDF5 physical estimate backend: implementation refinement

## Decision

A bounded, optional physical HDF5 estimate backend is feasible after the HDF5
metadata/lifecycle-hook candidate has passed its remaining r3 gates, received
independent review, and been integrated.  It should be a new
`estimates-io-hdf5` cross-project with only downward dependencies on
`estimates`, `estimates-io`, and `archive-hdf5`.

The accepted archive adapter remains an explicit native-provider dependency.
This proposal does not make HDF5 a default store, change `EstimateSink` or
`EstimateSource`, add a fit dependency, or qualify JDK 21, Linux, general
native concurrency, scientific inference, or production distribution.

## Immediate gate and candidate status

The current hook worktree is at `b11d1909ac36bc4e732a1224605f1f90c5113798`,
with the ten hook paths uncommitted.  Its r3 checks and independent review are
still pending.  That is a hard sequencing gate: no physical-backend writer or
new runtime receipt should start against this source.

Subject to that gate, the candidate has the minimum needed contract:

- `Hdf5Representation` and `Hdf5PayloadLayout` validate the full physical
  inventory, including ordered product/observation coverage and the compact
  shared-upper-triangle constraint.
- `LocalEstimateStore.publishHdf5Unit` is the metadata-only publication hook;
  it deliberately requires the physical backend to close and re-inspect its
  datasets first.
- `verifyEstimability`, `publishStagedIdempotent`, and
  `inspectWithRepresentations` supply the existing local-store lifecycle
  pieces without widening the default NIfTI route.
- `LocalEstimateCollections` is injectable at `private[io]`, so an HDF-only
  collection inspector can own publish/open/current/discover and CAS without
  a mixed-backend collection.
- The candidate refuses HDF5 from NIfTI sources and refuses inference evidence
  from an HDF5 unit before any physical payload is admitted.

No additional public lifecycle hook is needed.  The new backend may use
`private[io]` access from `scalafim.estimates.io.hdf5`; it must not expose or
subclass `LocalEstimateStore` merely to reach those hooks.

## Assigned module and paths

Add one explicit opt-in cross-project; do not modify existing estimate public
interfaces or ordinary aggregate aliases.

```text
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateLimits.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateLayout.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateBackend.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateStore.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateSink.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateSource.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateBackendPlatform.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/js/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateBackendPlatform.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/shared/src/test/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateLayoutSuite.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/test/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateStoreSuite.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/test/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimatePhysicalFixtureSuite.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/js/src/test/scala/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/Hdf5EstimateBackendSuite.scala
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/test/resources/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/h5py_oracle.py
modules/estimates-io-hdf5/jvm/src/test/resources/scalafim/estimates/io/hdf5/h5py_oracle_expected.json
build.sbt
README.md
docs/module-relations.md
docs/verification/estimate-hdf5-physical-<date>.md
```

`Hdf5EstimateBackend` is a small shared capability facade whose platform object
is supplied by both `jvm` and `js` source roots.  The shared facade accepts no
JVM `Path`, `LocalEstimateStore`, or other JVM-only type.  Its Scala.js
platform implementation must return a typed `EstimateError.Unsupported` before
any native/archive operation.  Its JVM platform implementation delegates to
the JVM-only `Hdf5EstimateStore.open`, which accepts the explicit archive
capability, local root, and validated `Hdf5EstimateLimits`.  The returned
objects implement only existing reader/sink contracts; the facade does not
introduce another scientific schema or a fit-facing API.

In `build.sbt`, `estimatesIoHdf5` must depend only on
`estimates`, `estimatesIo`, and `archiveHdf5`.  It is excluded from ordinary
`scalafimCompileAll` and default test aliases.  Its JVM tests are invoked only
with the explicit, pre-existing verified HDF provider cache property.  The JS
module may compile and run capability-refusal tests without a provider.

## Physical representation and bounded resources

`Hdf5EstimateLayout` derives all payload shape from the existing
`ProductDescriptor`, ordered observation axes, and existing selection types;
it stores no duplicate scientific axes in a new schema.

- Per-sample products have `/values` and `/validity` with extent
  `[observation, target, sample]`.  `target` is the estimand width for scalar
  products and the existing ordered upper-triangle width for
  `AbsolutePerSample` covariance.
- Compact shared U has `/values` and `/validity` with extent
  `[observation, pair]`.  Only `writeSharedCovariance` can write it, and it
  retains the existing normalized, Float64, sample-invariant validation.
- `/values` uses the descriptor-selected physical dtype; `/validity` is U8.
  Conversion from the existing `Array[Double]` caller buffer is slab-bounded.
- Cross-plane inference evidence is not represented.  The backend must refuse
  an evidence-bearing profile with `EstimateError.Unsupported` before staging,
  native acquisition, or a partial catalog write.

The backend uses a restrictive `Hdf5Limits` profile with:

```text
maxBlockElements       65,536
rawCacheBytes          1 MiB
metadataCacheBytes     4 MiB
maxFiles               1 per active product transaction
maxDatasetsPerFile     2 (/values and /validity)
```

“Two-handle admission” must mean two payload datasets per file.  It must not
be stated as two native identifiers: the archive adapter's valid native-ID
limit has a higher minimum and also covers file, space, and cleanup IDs.  The
backend uses the adapter's compatible bounded native-ID limit and closes every
scope through its supplied resource helper.

A private coverage ledger is finite and validated before allocation.  Its
configured byte cap is independent of the 4 MiB metadata cache cap and must be
included in `Hdf5EstimateLimits`; a request exceeding that ledger is refused.
The implementation may stream selection slabs, but may never expand a complete
plane, complete sample domain, or full covariance payload into memory.

## Writer and reader lifecycle

The JVM sink implements existing `EstimateSink` and `SharedCovarianceSink`.
It is caller-owned and one product transaction is active at a time.

1. Begin validates the full unit, representation inventory, absence of
   inference evidence, estimability references, limits, and the staging name.
   It uses exclusive creation, never truncate or overwrite.
2. Before a write, validate the existing `EstimateSelection` or
   `SharedCovarianceSelection`, Long arithmetic, destination capacity, layout,
   and coverage range.  Write values and validity as bounded slabs; mark the
   private coverage ledger only after both writes succeed.
3. `seal` requires full coverage.  It closes the file/datasets, reopens it
   read-only, and checks exactly two datasets, expected extents/dtypes/chunks,
   and no foreign payload path.  Only then can it call
   `publishStagedIdempotent` and `publishHdf5Unit`.
4. A separate HDF-only `LocalEstimateCollections` inspector owns
   publish/open/current/discover and the compare-and-swap pointer.  It verifies
   the selected published generation before publishing the new pointer.
5. `abort` is idempotent and closes all acquired resources.  Failure, cancel,
   duplicate publication, stale CAS, or reinspection failure leaves neither a
   catalog publication nor a current-pointer advance.

`Hdf5EstimateSource` is separately caller-owned.  It opens read-only only
through the HDF-only metadata profile, validates representation and shape
before returning data, reads caller selections as slabs, and closes all owned
resources exactly once.  It does not fall through to `NiftiEstimateSource` or
mix HDF/NIfTI collection entries.

## Required evidence before any adoption claim

After the hook candidate is accepted and integrated, the new backend requires:

1. Shared tests for layout derivation, descriptor/dtype selection, ordered
   axes, compact-U refusal paths, coverage-cap refusal, evidence refusal, and
   JVM/JS typed missing-capability behavior.
2. JVM native fixtures that independently inspect each produced file with the
   owned `h5py_oracle.py` generator/checker and literal
   `h5py_oracle_expected.json` resource: `/values` and `/validity` names,
   dtype, rank, extents, chunk shape, ordered values, validity bytes,
   reverse/slab selection behavior, and a reopen after seal.  Fixture files
   must cover per-sample scalar, absolute-covariance, and compact shared-U
   products.  The Scala test must invoke the owned checker against the emitted
   file; it must not treat a Scala-produced expectation as the oracle.
3. JVM lifecycle controls for close-before-publish, reinspection failure,
   cancellation, late callback, stale CAS, duplicate/no-clobber, and resource
   disposal.  Tests must exercise pre-native Long dimension/offset/count and
   caller-buffer failures, rather than relying on native exceptions.
4. A resource receipt demonstrating every request uses at most 65,536 cells,
   no payload cache over 1 MiB, no metadata cache over 4 MiB, and no more than
   two payload datasets per active file.  It must distinguish adapter native
   identifier bounds from the two-dataset contract.
5. Actual opt-in JVM and shared/JS receipts, source/provider/classpath closure,
   and an independent review of the physical files and failure controls.
   Ordinary no-provider compilation remains a separate gate and must continue
   to avoid fetch/load/native initialization.

## Remaining limits

This scope supports only the two existing physical payload families.  It does
not add inference evidence, status/plane fabrication, estimate codecs,
pooled/legacy migration, fit dependencies, scientific qualification, sustained
throughput evidence, JDK 21 or Linux evidence, native race guarantees, or
publication/durability claims beyond the tested local store lifecycle.
set.title: Implement and qualify bounded opt-in physical HDF5 estimate backend
